defense_in_depth_findings.title: Runtime wrapper validate_release does not itself verify release-document accounting or preserved-semantics sections
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: In an isolated committed-byte-derived workspace, a release copy with accounting.future_s2_constructions tampered from 1 to 2 passed wrapper v2 validate_release (which checks schema, identity, state, stop_boundary, and binding hashes but not the release document's own accounting/semantics sections or its whole-file hash). The tamper was rejected by the committed validator v2 (INVALID:preserved v1 semantics accounting, exit 2) and by validate_approval (ReleaseError:APPROVAL_RELEASE, since approval.release_sha256 is checked against sha256_path(RELEASE) before any attempt authority exists); the future go token binds the same release_sha256 transitively.
defense_in_depth_findings.required_action: NON_BLOCKING_ACCEPTED: no execution authority is obtainable through the gap because validate_approval whole-file-hashes the release against the committed approval constant 1182257c... before attempt start, the machine-local go token must bind the identical release_sha256, and the committed validator independently rejects the tamper. Recommend a future append-only revision add a release-document whole-file hash check (or the validator's preserved-semantics section checks) to the runtime wrapper's validate_release so the earliest gate also fails closed.

statement: REPRESENTATIVE S2 SINGLE-USE RELEASE V2 APPROVAL ACCEPTED. Verified against committed bytes at 184ba3b961b393b8a5608f2b599a180045156685 only; no machine-local S1/FFN operand, checkpoint, shard, attempt-state, or token path was read or written, no attempt or S2 start was created, no S2 arithmetic was executed, and no GO token was minted. The committed approval artifact recomputes to sha256 c6ccffc3... and carries exactly the ordered 28-field census of the committed v2 approval contract (independently re-parsed with duplicate-key rejection; ordered list equality confirmed) with every required constant matching, including verdict ACCEPT, exact approval statement REPRESENTATIVE S2 SINGLE-USE RELEASE V2 APPROVED, approval_does_not_execute true, approval_is_not_go_token true, real_event_authorized false, ledger 175 (independently reproduced by executing the committed ledger adapter against the committed ledger-175 source document), zero checkpoint/shard/S1-materialization/FFN-composition budgets, exactly one future S2 construction, and stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_S2_OUTPUT_ONLY. All bound hashes were recomputed from committed bytes and match: release v2 1182257c..., construction authorization b85b255f..., arithmetic contract abbf1583..., release review 79016f23... at the enforced v2 review path, approval contract v2 fd97ad9b... as pinned inside the release; execution_code_head 33d0355c and release reviewed_head d2590ce are both commits ancestral to the review target, and the release bytes at d2590ce hash identically to the approval-bound release_sha256. The bound release review carries reviewer identity CLAUDE_FABLE_5_INDEPENDENT_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWER and model claude-fable-5, verdict ACCEPT with empty blocking and non-blocking-required arrays and three defense-in-depth findings each holding a concrete non-blocking disposition, and the approval's approver identity CLAUDE_FABLE_5_INDEPENDENT_APPROVER / model claude-fable-5 is distinct from the release reviewer identity. Transitive lineage verified: the construction authorization pinned by the approval binds the exact accepted singular S1 producer manifest 9ddf842c... (schema pulsarmlx.f017.representative-s1-private-manifest, singular-artifact-object-only census, producer role LAYER3_POST_ATTENTION_RESIDUAL, artifact 8309377e..., f32le [6144]/24576 bytes) and the distinct FFN producer manifest 0f6a887f... (one-element artifacts array, symbolic_path, artifact 4d7aaeb5..., f64le [6144]/49152 bytes), matching the release's operand_manifest_contracts and operands sections byte-for-byte; release v1 (1b05c093...) remains superseded for execution authority per the release's v1_disposition and the bound supersession record dbc73f9f..., with v1 go tokens prohibited and none ever committed. The authority chain is acyclic and strictly commit-ordered: release v2 banked at d2590ce, independent review banked at 9dcc656, approval banked at 184ba3b, each artifact committed exactly once, with the future machine-local go token bound only transitively through the exact approval sha256 and carrying a disjoint 8-field census. The actual committed gates were exercised on committed-byte-derived temporary copies only: the committed validator v2 accepted the release under pinned CPython 3.14.6, and the committed wrapper v2 validate_release and validate_approval both passed in a detached committed-bytes worktree. An adversarial battery of 33 substitutions was rejected fail-closed by the committed gates: missing/extra/reordered fields and duplicate keys (APPROVAL_EXACT_FIELDS_AND_ORDER, DUPLICATE_KEY), v1-copied approval bytes (APPROVAL_CONSTANTS), stale-v1 and forged release hashes (APPROVAL_RELEASE), wrong reviewed head (REVIEWED_HEAD), wrong review path and wrong review sha (REVIEW_PATH, REVIEW_SHA), physically tampered review bytes (REVIEW_SHA), physically tampered release bytes (validator preserved-semantics rejection and APPROVAL_RELEASE), wrong authorization and arithmetic hashes (APPROVAL_CONTRACT_BINDING), wrong code head (APPROVAL_CODE_HEAD), wrong reviewer/approver identities and models, nonzero budgets, two future constructions, wrong ledger, altered stop boundary, REJECT verdict, forged statement, real_event_authorized flip, and execute/token flag flips (all APPROVAL_CONSTANTS), and the approval document itself presented as a GO token (TOKEN_EXACT_FIELDS_AND_ORDER); any reserialization of the approval changes its sha256 away from c6ccffc3..., severing token binding. One defense-in-depth finding is recorded with a concrete non-blocking disposition. The approval safely completes the release-to-review-to-approval segment of the authority chain without itself executing anything or functioning as a GO token.
